findings.where: Hero, first screen, desktop and phone: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it
findings.fault: The page's one action is dead. 'Write to me' is a filled blue button with a hover rule, and the address next to it is underlined, but neither does anything when clicked: both are static in the parts map, and neither is a mailto link. The only working contact is the small address in the footer, after the whole style tile.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to contact Mark clicks the button, then the address, and nothing happens. They have to copy the address by hand or give up. Getting in touch is the page's one job (brand sheet §1), so this stops the task.

findings.where: Hero, first screen: the second filled blue button, 'Book a consultation' (links to #consult), next to 'Write to me'
findings.fault: Two filled buttons in the same colour sit side by side, so the first screen has two primary actions where the brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark. 'Book a consultation' jumps to #consult, and no consultation or booking section appears anywhere in the render, so it suggests a booking service the site doesn't offer. It is also the only one of the two buttons that does anything, which pulls visitors away from the personal contact.
findings.who_objects: A visitor can't tell which button is the real way in. If they pick 'Book a consultation', they get no booking form and no calendar. The founder would object too, because the personal-advisor test asks for one direct way to reach Mark and the brochure-site rule (brand sheet §6) rules out booking software.

findings.where: Hero margin notes ('Istanbul, 2025 / Best Practices in PPP Legislation for Emerging Economies', 'Melbourne, 2026 / LLM Course on PPP Law…', 'São Paulo, 2024 / New Approaches to Risk Allocation…'), plus the blue section labels below the fold (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The margin notes name specific talks and courses and are set in the house blue that the page's own palette reserves for links. A talk title in link colour reads as a link to that talk, but every note is static. The same blue also marks the working footer link and the PDF row, so on this page one look means both 'link' and 'label'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to see Mark's Istanbul or São Paulo talk clicks the blue title and nothing happens. They learn that blue can't be trusted to mean 'link', which also weakens the real links on the page.
